description.value: A multilevel whole-brain fMRI mediation study examining how price cues alter experienced taste pleasantness through activity in valuation and affective-regulation regions, with a follow-up moderated mediation analysis using independent monetary reward sensitivity.

spans.text: We used a whole-brain multilevel mediation approach with healthy participants who tasted identical wines cued with different prices while their brains were scanned using fMRI.

description.value: Observational experimental study with healthy participants assigned to repeated within-participant wine price-cue and payment conditions across three fMRI sessions and additional behavioral sessions over two weeks.

spans.text: The experiment consisted of four events spread over two weeks (Fig.  1a ).
Taken together, we applied a 3 (bottle price €3, €6, €18) × 2 (pay/no pay) within-participant experimental design.

spans.text: In this task, participants were instructed that their goal was to win as much money as possible by finding a circle in one out of a varying number of boxes displayed on the screen.
Participants saw the information via goggles and indicated their responses using a response box system (both NNL, Bergen, Norway).
That is, when participants guessed the right box as containing the circle, they were rewarded with a payoff of 10 cents; otherwise they won nothing.

spans.text: We used this task because it allowed us to adapt the task difficulty to each individual’s performance by varying the tilt.
Participants saw the information via goggles and indicated their responses using a response box system (both NNL, Bergen, Norway).
In other words, the task difficulty was adjusted such that the performance of each participant was around 60% to 65% correct answers.

model_settings.value: Single-trial regressors modeled 3-second wine-tasting responses; nuisance regressors included run intercepts, linear drift, 24 head-motion regressors, wine type and payment condition; trials with VIF ≥2.5 were excluded; mediation significance was tested with 10,000-observation bootstrap confidence intervals.

spans.text: A general linear model (GLM) design matrix estimated the magnitude of single-trial responses at the time of wine tasting (boxcar durations: 3 seconds) with separate regressors for each trial.
Importantly, the current study used a multilevel mediation analysis, which accounts for both within- and between-participant variations by treating participant as a random effect.
This involved estimating the distribution of individual path coefficients by randomly sampling with replacement 10,000 observations from the matrix of [a, b, c, c’, a × b] path coefficients.
Multilevel mediation analysis was conducted using the Mediation Toolbox (  https://github.com/canlab/CanlabScripts  ).
price cue
We considered only the contrasts between the two extreme price cue conditions for the predictor variable   x   (e.g., €18 vs. €3).
Taken together, we applied a 3 (bottle price €3, €6, €18) × 2 (pay/no pay) within-participant experimental design.
Note that the effect of price cue was linear across the three price conditions, replicating prior work .
payment condition

We had two experimental conditions: (1) We manipulated the bottle price information given to participants in each trial (i.e., €3, €6, €18), and (2) we manipulated whether participants could sample the wines for free or whether they had to pay a price that was 10% of the indicated bottle price (i.e., €0.3, €0.6, or €1.8).
